name: Kepler-78B

boundTo.source: El-Badry, Rix & Heintz (2021, MNRAS 506, 2269) list Kepler-78 and Kepler-78B in their Gaia EDR3 wide-binary catalogue (VizieR J/MNRAS/506/2269, source_id 2078373642776670080 and 2078373642781135744), 921 AU apart on the sky, with a chance-alignment probability of 1.5e-5: the pair is bound. No orbit of the pair is published, and the Gaia astrometry alone does not constrain one, so the star is placed by its own astrometry and carries no orbit.

description: Star bound to Kepler-78, 921 AU away.

radius.source: Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the radius of TIC 270701666 (VizieR IV/39/tic82)

mass.source: Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the mass of TIC 270701666 (VizieR IV/39/tic82)

temperature.source: Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the effective temperature of TIC 270701666 (VizieR IV/39/tic82)

text.card: Kepler-78B is a star of 3,369 K, bound to Kepler-78 921 AU away.
text.introduction: Kepler-78B shares its motion through space with Kepler-78, 921 AU away, so the two are a bound pair. Both are placed where Gaia measures them.

notes: Kepler-78B's orbit around Kepler-78 is not measured; both stars are placed at their Gaia DR3 positions, which is where they are

radialVelocity.source: No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 2078373642781135744 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 40,000 of its distance per century
